record.original_question: Fix an integer n > 2. Define Phi_G on subsets S of the vertex set V of an undirected graph G = (V, E) by Phi_G(S) = S union {v in V | there exist distinct s0, s1 in S with {s0, v} and {s1, v} both edges of G}. A graph is propagative if for every two-element subset S of V there exists k >= 1 such that Phi_G^k(S) = V. Determine the smallest integer m such that every undirected graph with n vertices and minimum degree at least m is necessarily propagative.

evidence.quote: We call G propagative if, for any S subset V with |S| = 2, there exists k >= 1 such that Phi^k S = V.
Puzzle 3.1.2. Fix n > 2. Find the minimum m such that any undirected graph G = (V, E) with - |V| = n, and - each v in V has degree at least m is necessarily propagative.
This bound is in fact sharp; that is, the answer to Puzzle 3.1.2 is m = floor(n/2) + 1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G = (V, E)$ be a finite simple undirected graph. For a subset $S \subseteq V$, define
$$\Phi_G(S) = S \cup \{v \in V : \text{there exist distinct } s_0, s_1 \in S \text{ with } \{s_0,v\}, \{s_1,v\} \in E\}.$$
Iterate $\Phi_G$ by $\Phi_G^{k+1}(S) = \Phi_G(\Phi_G^k(S))$ with $\Phi_G^0(S) = S$. Call $G$ propagative if for every two-element subset $S \subseteq V$ there exists $k \geq 1$ such that $\Phi_G^k(S) = V$.

Fix an integer $n > 2$. Determine the smallest integer $m = m(n)$ such that every simple undirected graph on $n$ vertices in which every vertex has degree at least $m$ is necessarily propagative.
artifact.status_search_result: The parsed source states the answer is $m = \lfloor n/2 \rfloor + 1$, presented with a sharpness claim. No independent corroboration was sought, but the problem is presented as resolved in its original venue.
